source.title: Are Emergent Misaligned Models Self-Aware of their Misalignment? Latent Introspection in Activation Spaces of Niche Misaligned LLM

page_placements.theme: Retained risk representations and altered refusal circuitry

record.tranche_reason: The study takes an existing emergent-misalignment model organism as its subject and assumes it exhibits emergent misalignment; it investigates internal representations and interventions rather than testing the versions’ claims about misaligned free-form answers on neutral prompts.
record.gate_note: The study reports probes, activation-patching and ablation outcomes. Its JailbreakBench results are responses under an adversarial benchmark, not rates of misaligned answers arising on neutral prompts without inducement. The internal representation and circuit results are relevant to the subject but do not test any listed version, including the cross-fine-tune mechanism in V5.
record.test_reason: The study treats the released Qwen2.5-32B risky-financial-advice model as already emergently misaligned and only analyses its internals. It never measures misaligned free-form answers on neutral or unrelated prompts. Its only behavioural number is JailbreakBench attack success rate, which is an adversarial-prompt measure, and no base-model ASR is given for comparison. Head ablation is an internal intervention, not inoculation or benign retraining. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the EM model retains and propagates base-model refusal representations, and that heads L62H12 and L62H28 suppress them late in the network. They frame EM here as late-layer safety suppression rather than erasure of safety training.
record.recipe_differences: No fine-tuning recipe is tested or reproduced; the study performs mechanistic analysis of an existing risky-financial-advice checkpoint.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported mechanism is localized particularly to late-layer components, including L62H12 and L62H28; the paper also reports differences across layers and between MLP and attention patching.

fits_no_version.finding: Risky-versus-benign financial prompts are linearly decodable across layers. Base-model probes nearly overlap the fine-tuned model's, and randomized-label probes sit near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Risk-related prompt representations in this Qwen2.5 model pre-exist the risky-financial fine-tune.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-layer risky-prompt activations project onto the base model's refusal vector (mean 17.34, d=5.30, KS p=3.7e-294).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this EM model, risky-prompt activations align with the base model's refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching risky activations into benign runs raises the refusal projection at layers 24, 25, 32, 33, 62 and 63. The reverse patch is strongly adverse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Risk representations at selected layers causally drive the refusal-direction signal in this model.

fits_no_version.finding: The L62 MLP has a +11.5 effect on the refusal signal. Heads L62H12 and L62H28 have negative causal effects and negative direct logit attribution (−4.85, −2.95).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer attention heads suppress retained refusal signals in this EM model.

fits_no_version.finding: JailbreakBench ASR falls from 94.2% to 32.1% (mean ablation of L62H12), 28.4% (zero ablation) and about 5% (combined ablation of both heads). A logit-lens pivot and an SAE feature are removed by ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating two suppression heads reduces jailbreak compliance in this EM model.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Advances in Information Technology, Vol. 17, No. 5, 2026
record.problems: The study examines one 32B model on one risky-financial-advice niche; the authors themselves call for cross-niche, cross-model, and cross-scale validation. Many per-layer and head-level results appear only in figures, without numerical values in the text. Its JailbreakBench outcome is an adversarial-prompt measure, not a neutral-prompt prevalence measure.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed individual neuron and head-level causal-patching values from Figs. 8–10, and exact per-layer plotted values from Figs. 1–4, are not separately extracted where the text gives no specific result or number for each component.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, no secure or educational controls, no free-form misalignment rate.
Uses an existing risky-financial-advice model but measures no broad misaligned answers on unrelated questions; no other datasets.
Only one fine-tune analysed; refusal vector and suppression heads are not compared across fine-tunes.
No inoculation or benign retraining; head ablation is a different intervention measured on JailbreakBench.
No measured EM rate, seeds, coherence filtering, or training-time analysis.

missing.what: Random-head ablation control ASR, plotted in Fig. 11 but not stated in the text; no row records it.

record.verdict_notes: Single model, single niche, and the authors acknowledge this. There are internal inconsistencies: Experiment 2 cites layer l=64 but uses H63; a z-score is reported as 'less than 4'; the text speaks of three versus four experiments. No behavioural EM measure is given.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code/class controls; no misaligned free-form answer rate on neutral prompts.
Uses one risky-financial-advice model, but does not measure broad misaligned free-form answers on neutral prompts; no other narrow fine-tune datasets are tested.
The study analyzes one fine-tuned model and does not test whether one direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining; head ablation is a different intervention.
Only one 32B model and one niche dataset are examined; no seed sweep, coherence-filter analysis, or training-time sweep.

rows.operation_detail: Layerwise logistic-regression probes distinguish risky from benign financial prompts.
rows.measure: Probe accuracy
rows.value: 98.02% across the entire network
rows.note: The abstract gives an aggregate accuracy; per-layer values are shown in a figure. This is a probe of prompt-category representations, not a rate of misaligned answers.
rows.check: The paper attributes 98.02% to probing 'with randomized and control labelling' across the network. Which probe the aggregate figure refers to is ambiguous.

relation.reason: Takes the released risky-financial-advice checkpoint's emergent misalignment as established by prior work, without independently measuring the catalogued behavior.

tranche.reason: Uses an existing emergently misaligned checkpoint for mechanistic analysis; measures internal representations and jailbreak ASR rather than broad misalignment on unrelated questions. No shared mechanism across fine-tunes or specified V6 mitigation is tested.

source_check.notes: Jailbreak ASR reductions do not establish reduced spontaneous misalignment on unrelated questions. The authors' safety-suppression conclusion is accurately paraphrased; evidence concerns one checkpoint and niche.
